prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline;Arrival Regulation Console=Nightjar(help-only). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages;Marlinstone forecasts. Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Capacity Assessment Module updates Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector constraints. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;freeze:Pushback Window Token. Capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Halcyon confirms publication/compliance;Aircraft Operator Representative readiness;changes justified. Foxglove role-restricted;stands cannot override airspace. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:movements/milestones≤5s;validated occupancy/equipment-status→Skylark/Ironleaf. Quartzline→Blueharbor:Stand Tow Request Form;Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Brindle advisory-only. Recovery Phase/Contingency Fallback State:safe diversion/prioritization/communication/recovery;Saffron confirms plan/short-deferral/revised-intent. Handling Resource Planner grades severity/suppresses recovery duplicates;Ground Handling Dispatcher→Towbar Shortage Report. Performance Analytics Warehouse compares escalations/actual off-block performance:tunes severity,reduces nuisance. Adverse Weather

New part:
S554: If a bus shortage or terminal loading delay is detected, the Airline Operations Coordinator may request revision of the Target Off Block Time before the delay propagates to runway demand.
S555: The Regional Flow Manager considers repeated remote stand transfer delays as an input to tactical capacity assessment during peak arrival and departure banks.
S556: Ramp Control Lead uses the Towbar Shortage Report to determine whether remote stand aircraft can be repositioned without creating secondary apron congestion.
S557: The Capacity Assessment Module reflects persistent remote stand service limits as a reduction in practical gate throughput rather than only as a ramp movement issue.
S558: The Gate Conflict Detector identifies cases where an aircraft assigned to a contact gate would cause less overall delay than a nominally available remote stand with inadequate passenger transfer capacity.
S559: When remote stand use increases, the Airport CDM Portal records the operational reason, affected flights, expected passenger transfer duration, and responsible control position.
S560: The Common Situation Display presents remote stand status in time order so that airline, ramp, tower, and airport roles share the same expectation for aircraft readiness.
S561: Landside service limits are linked to airside timing through estimated boarding completion, bus return availability, crew access, and terminal processing constraints.
S562: A remote stand departure is not considered ready for push or tow until passengers, bags, crew, and required ground services are aligned with the planned aircraft movement.
S563: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Airport Duty Manager may reduce planned remote stand use because bus loading, walking routes, and accessible transfer times become less predictable.
S564: During Recovery Phase, remote stands may be used to absorb late arrivals while preserving contact gates for flights with tight turnarounds or high connection sensitivity.
S565: The Performance Analytics Warehouse retains remote stand timing measures so that planners can compare scheduled assumptions with actual passenger transfer and apron release performance.
S566: This section extends the remote stand performance concept by describing how border, customs, and apron sensing inputs become constraints in the daily operating plan.
S567: Border release status is represented as a readiness attribute on each affected flight record in the Regional Flow Platform, separate from aircraft readiness and airline commercial readiness.
S568: The Airport Duty Manager produces the Customs Hold Release Note when border processing confirms that a held arrival may proceed to normal turnaround handling.
S569: Customs hold indicators are represented as operational constraints that prevent premature stand release, passenger transfer assumptions, or departure readiness claims.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
